mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries with identical content to exist as distinct atoms. Alloy can then instantiate a universe where two audit entries record the same event, violating the append-only immutability invariant that AppendOnly and FR_017 check for.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateAuditEntry { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.task_id = ae2.task_id and ae1.operation = ae2.operation and ae1.actor_user_id = ae2.actor_user_id and ae1.actor_role = ae2.actor_role and ae1.diff_summary = ae2.diff_summary }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a task to exist without any audit entry, particularly without a Created entry. The AuditCompleteness assertion verifies that every task has at least a creation audit entry; without the constraining fact, a counterexample (task with no audit) becomes satisfiable.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TaskWithoutAudit { some t: Task | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.task_id = t }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact permits users from one team to have access (ownership or sharing) to tasks in another team. The NoInformationLeakage and FR_006 assertions enforce that such cross-team access is impossible; without the constraint, Alloy can find a counterexample (user from team A is sharee or owner of a task in team B).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamAccess { some t: Task, u: User | u.team_id != t.team_id and (u in t.shared_with or u = t.owner_id) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a task to have an owner from a different team than the task itself. OwnershipBasedAccess and FR_009 assert that owners are in the same team; without the constraint, a counterexample (owner.team_id != task.team_id) satisfies the formula.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnerXTeam { some t: Task | t.owner_id.team_id != t.team_id }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows in-team members (non-owners) to access tasks they do not own and are not shared on. OwnershipBasedAccess asserts that such members must be in the shared_with set to access; without the constraint, a member can be unshared yet still implicitly allowed access.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MemberAccessUnsharedTask { some t: Task, u: User | u.role = Member and u.team_id = t.team_id and u != t.owner_id and u not in t.shared_with }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact permits users from different teams to be added to the shared_with list of a task. FR_012 and NoInformationLeakage assert that all sharees are in the task's team; without the constraint, a counterexample (sharee.team_id != task.team_id) becomes possible.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_XTeamSharee { some t: Task, s: t.shared_with | s.team_id != t.team_id }
